1.note: A pun. In Num 12:14 יָרֹק יָרַק בְּפָנֶיהָ means "(her father) spat in her face"; here יָרָק is "greenery" and יָרַק is read as "grew green".

2.note: Barak, the judge of Judg 4–5, is also בָּרָק "lightning". The cloud is Deborah, the thunder and rain are her army, and the scene borrows the verses of Judg 4–5.

3.note: A play on two words of nearly the same letters: נְשָׁמוֹת "souls" and נְשַׁמּוֹת "desolate".

4.he: יוּכַל בַּעְלָהּ הָרִאשׁוֹן אֲשֶׁר שִׁלְּחָהּ לָשׁוּב לְקַחְתָּהּ
4.note: Deut 24:4 says the first husband "may not" (לֹא יוּכַל) take back his divorced wife after she has married another. The negation is dropped: Nisan, the earth's first husband, may take her back from winter.

5.note: The Ludim are a son of Mizraim (Egypt) in Gen 10:13; here they stand for the Egyptians, for the rhyme.

6.note: Lev 1:9 (the burnt offering) and Lev 6:21 (the vessel scoured after a sin offering): the drowning of Pharaoh is told in the language of washing a sacrifice.

7.note: Ruth 1:21 has ה' (the Lord); here the cup says אֲדֹנַי, pointed as the divine name, but meaning the drinker, "my lord", who has emptied it.

8.note: Read as נֵס "banner" with a suffix, "their banner", made to rhyme with נִיסָן. Uncertain.

9.note: Iyyar was held to be a month of healing; a later tradition reads its letters as the initials of אֲנִי ה' רֹפְאֶךָ (Exod 15:26). The feminine "which cheers" (הַמְשַׂמַּחַת) seems to go with "healing"; in Judg 9:13 the words are said of wine.

10.note: Lev 14:37 describes the marks of leprosy in the walls of a house; here the same words describe the green and red patches of new growth on the ground.

11.note: שָׁלִישִׁים are "captains" or "officers" (Exod 14:7, 2 Kgs 9:25), but the word also means "third ones": Sivan is the third month, and its praise is given by the third poet.

12.note: Kaminka's edition (p. 59) reads מכסות אור, "covered with light", for מְכֻסּוֹת דַּר, "covered with pearl"; the translation follows the Ben-Yehuda text. The Ben-Yehuda text of this gate ends after this line; the rest of the gate is taken from Kaminka (see note 13).

13.note: This passage is missing from the Ben-Yehuda text and is taken from Kaminka's edition (Warsaw 1899, pp. 59–69), unvocalized. It runs from the second line of the poem on Sivan to the end of the gate.

14.note: Ezek 8:14 tells of women "weeping for the Tammuz", a Mesopotamian god; here the congregations weep in the month Tammuz, over the breaking of the tablets and the breach of Jerusalem's wall (both on 17 Tammuz, m. Taanit 4:6).

15.note: Kaminka prints יומי, which reads as a poetic form of "its days"; the summer days of Av are long.

16.note: A pun: מְשֻׁקָּדִים in Exod 25:33 are the almond-shaped cups of the lampstand; here the almonds are "almonded", in bloom. Each pair in this line rhymes the fruit with its praise.

17.note: Gen 44:20, the brothers to Joseph: "we have an old father". אָב is also the month Av, which has grown old with mourning. The 1,150 years since the destruction of the Temple (70 CE) give about 1220, the time al-Ḥarizi wrote the book. The "father" and the "wise son" (wine) play on the month's name through the rest of the passage; Kaminka's footnote explains אב as "the month Av".

18.note: Kaminka prints מקלטת clearly; the word is taken as "takes in, absorbs" (קלט). Perhaps a misprint of מלקטת, "gathers up".

19.note: Kaminka prints ופרע; the translation follows the parallel "worship" and "do homage" (perhaps read וכרע, "bow down"). Isa 44:19 mocks the man who bows "to a block of wood" (לְבוּל עֵץ); here בּוּל is the fruit of the field, and also the old name of the eighth month (1 Kgs 6:38).

20.note: The calendar rules by which certain feasts may not fall on certain weekdays (for example, Rosh Hashanah not on Sunday, Wednesday or Friday) are fixed from Tishri.

21.note: A pun: חֶשְׁבּוֹן in Num 21:28 is the city Heshbon; here it is the "account" a man gives of his deeds. Kaminka prints בציד; read בציר, "in pangs" (ד and ר are close in this print).

22.note: Kaminka's print can be read וכוסה or ובוסה; the sense needs וכוסה, "its cup". ראויה ("fitting") may stand for רְוָיָה, "overflowing" (Ps 23:5).

23.note: צִיר "pang" and צֳרִי "balm" have the same letters.

24.he: כי בה תפלם לך נתיבות גיל בידי יגונות הזמן ענן
24.note: Kaminka prints תפלם, taken as תְּפַלֵּס "level" (Prov 4:26, 5:6); עִנָּן, "afflicted them", is rendered freely as "made hard". Uncertain.

25.he: כושית מבנות חם לובשת מעשה פחם
25.note: The Cushite woman is the fire of coals in the brazier: black as coal, "of the daughters of Ham" (חָם, also "hot"), and fighting the cold.

26.note: Gen 5:29, Lamech naming Noah. Noah planted the first vineyard (Gen 9:20), so wine is the comfort that was foretold.

27.note: Kaminka prints תכבדהו ("honor it"); the sense needs תכבהו, "quench it", and the translation follows that.

28.he: וחשוב דמיהם כמו נפש ולהם רוחך גו
28.note: The red wine is the "blood" of the cups (Kaminka's footnote), and "the blood is the soul" (Deut 12:23); your own spirit is only the body (גֵּו) that holds it.

29.note: שֵׁבֶט "rod" is also the month שְׁבָט.

30.note: Kaminka's print looks like למרוה or למרזה; read לְמָדוּהָ, "they learned it", which the rest of the line requires (ד and ר, ו and ז are close in this print).
